You are the lead/coordinator for caliper's road to v1 alpha (Storybook integration is the product's purpose). Read first: ~/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-caliper/memory/MEMORY.md (and the memories it links), ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/worker-contract.md (workers' rules and the pre-push gate), AGENTS.md, and ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/oracle-run/{REPORT,pattern-eval,pattern-eval-mui-radix,memory-split,memory-profile}.md. Date of this handoff: 2026-11-16.

## Product rule (the user's, non-negotiable)
Storybook Controls must list EVERYTHING in the component's main props even if no story uses it, plus whatever the component body itself uses directly (reads, destructures, passes explicitly; never through a DOM spread). Big generated/ambient sources (DOM/ARIA/event attributes, style-system props) stay as names in a layer. Decide by provenance and structure, never by name lists. Fix classes of problems and patterns, not one-off components ("produce the best results, not overwhelming numbers"). colorPalette staying hidden is fine. Say "the TypeScript checker (on by default)", not "add-on" (the exact wording sweep of docs/changesets is not done; confirm meaning first).
Alpha = someone installs the Storybook addon on a real design system and gets correct Controls fast on first and second start, with plain statements of what's missing; no stability/API freeze needed.

## Process rules
- Workers run in isolated worktrees; the lead pushes their branches (`git push origin <sha>:<branch>`, never force, merge main in rather than rebase), then `entire trail link 405 --branch <b> --base main --repo gh/orin-dx/caliper` (Entire opens the PR; don't `gh pr create` unless the user approves the shim/Touch ID). Publish bodies with `gh pr edit N --title ... --body-file ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/pr/<name>.md`. Trail 404 = Chakra memory regression, 405 = relevance/collapse/Storybook usefulness.
- Pre-push gate for workers: invariants in PR body, grammar sweep with the TS checker as oracle, mutation proofs, ALLOW-list guards, `/code-review medium` awaited, `just lint doc-check machete typos`, nextest, test-checker-lane when checker code changes. Lead reruns `just lint` itself (workers' sandbox blocks pnpm).
- After a verified fix, resolve the Entire finding yourself citing commit + test: `entire trail finding list caliper/<change> --freshness=any ...`. Findings for the same class: fix the class, not the case.
- Constraints: oracle/corpus runs cost money (only when asked; `scripts/weekly.py --oracle --corpus antd --corpus shadcn` is authorized for acceptance; never --agent-eval); no files in /tmp (use ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures or $TMPDIR); no new scripts/options without CI/weekly value; workers: Sonnet for mechanical, Opus for provenance/design, caps on tool calls, no polling CI, max 3 parallel workers; release actions (rerun, delete assets, re-dispatch, RELEASE_PENDING_FROM) need the user's say-so; measure peak RSS and time for resolver/checker changes; git inside worktree sessions: plain single commands, no `cd` to other worktrees, no compound `$(...)`.
- Never merge or release anything without the user's approval; the user approves/merges PRs.

## State
Merged on main: Chakra 42 GB fix, collapse default 'dependencies', scheduler S1/S2, factory own props, relevance output, #491 (instantiation memory), #489 (alpha limits docs), #487 (Wisp v5).
Open PRs (all BLOCKED on CI/approval at last look):
- #490 `feat/list-props-by-usage` (change 288, trail 405): T4 listing rule (main props + body use). Remote head cf51133b. Acceptance (oracle-run/accept/accept.sh) passed 5/5 on it: Storybook Button 21 rows (20 + children), Badge children/asChild/variant, shadcn 98.7%/0 wrong, antd 93.0%/1 wrong; differential 0 violations on 7 corpora; peak RSS shadcn 879 / Chakra 1,627 MiB. TWO OPEN ENTIRE FINDINGS (one class: explicit selection not seen by both owners): chain.rs:597-599 (checker keep-and-merge must include body-promoted notable props; types/semantic.rs LayerFacts::of / layer_notable) and relevance/props_type.rs:164-165 (substitute generic-alias args when collecting picked keys). A worker (agent ace6850035594237c, worktree .claude/worktrees/agent-ace6850035594237c, branch fix/list-rule-patterns) was mid-fix when the session ended; check its worktree (`git status`, `git log`), finish or restart: class fix with grammar sweep + model test that every visible structural row survives the checker merge + mutation proofs, then push to feat/list-props-by-usage and resolve both findings. Afterwards, separate commits: change 8 (no analysable body = unknown, keep what main listed: MUI .d.ts components lose className/style/ref), change 7 (hook hand-off useX(props) as forwarding), D (Chakra fixture still ~865 rows: the `declined` guard blocks the generated rule; decide if the guard is right). Evidence: pattern-eval.md lists 7 rule-level changes (1-6 done in #490: ambient by declaring interface, member ambient only if all declarations ambient, generated rule for project sources, reads promote from large layers, mapped-copy by key interface nature, one-hop aliases).
- #492 `fix/weekly-oracle-measurement` (change 290): Node heap 16 GB for Chakra oracle, "not judged" as its own column, headline over judged props, coverage floor 50% (new gate: ask the user whether it stays), recall counts layer names.
- Change 291 `perf/converter-memo-interning` (HEAD 1335c3d2 pushed, linked to trail 405): converter memo interning, Chakra peak 1,690 -> 1,366 MiB, output identical. NO PR was opened by Entire yet; check `gh pr list --head perf/converter-memo-interning --state all`; if still none ask the user (shim needs Touch ID). Publish body from ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/pr/perf-converter-memo-interning.md.
- #497 callisto/version-packages (release PR, not reviewed), #493-#496 dependabot.

## Next
1. Land #490's findings fix (above), push, check CI/Entire, resolve findings, rerun accept.sh on the new head: `zsh ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/oracle-run/accept/accept.sh <bin> <packages/storybook dir with napi build> <label>`; MUI/Radix: `oracle-run/pattern-eval/run-extra.sh <main-bin> <490-bin>`.
2. Chakra memory: ~1.1-1.2 GiB expected after #491 + memo interning; under 1 GiB needs more converter work (memory-split.md parts), not required for alpha.
3. Weekly: merge #492 then run the oracle once on merged main (idle machine), refresh docs/STATUS.md speed numbers; weekly "not judged" cause (Chakra 75.5%, Mantine 62.9%) undiagnosed.
4. Unmeasured: Storybook prefetch, antd in Storybook (Vite `./version` import fails), head-to-head vs react-docgen-typescript.
5. MUI `Button`/`Select` (OverridableComponent/ExtendButtonBase declare const) aren't extracted by either binary: separate extraction gap, ask the user if it should be a slice.

## Needs the user's decision (ask early)
- 0.11.0 release recovery (E167 ArtifactAssetDiffers): delete mismatched asset + `gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha=<sha>`, or skip via RELEASE_PENDING_FROM; is #497 the vehicle? (corpora budget gate never ran on a real release PR.)
- Should the addon default flip (collapseInheritedProps 'dependencies') ship in the first alpha? Alpha audience? Coverage floor on the weekly (#492)? Worktree cleanup: ~60 stale worktrees under .claude/worktrees (peer session cleanup-merged-branches-worktrees did a sweep; don't remove live ones).

Start by checking `gh pr list`, `gh pr checks 490`, Entire findings for caliper/288, 290, 291, and the worker worktree state, then continue with step 1 and report.

#!/bin/zsh
# Acceptance for a caliper build: CLI rows, Storybook Controls rows, oracle headline.
#   accept.sh <caliper-docgen binary> <packages/storybook dir (built: dist/, ../napi with its .node)> <label>
# Output: accept/out-<label>/ (cli/, sb/, weekly.json, accept-<label>.md). Exit 0 = every check passed.
# Env: SKIP_ORACLE=1 skips the oracle step (its check then fails: do not use for sign-off). WEEKLY overrides scripts/weekly.py.
# Timings come from a shared machine: not official. Playwright is the npm package in prefetch/drv (MCP tools cannot run
# from a script). Build the addon dir: git archive <sha> packages/storybook packages/napi, tsc in packages/storybook, and
# copy target/release/libcaliper_docgen_napi.dylib to packages/napi/caliper_docgen_napi.darwin-arm64.node
# (see build-d884334e/ for the layout).
set -u
HERE=${0:A:h}
BIN=${1:?binary}; ADDON=${2:?storybook dir}; LABEL=${3:?label}
FX=/Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures
WEEKLY=${WEEKLY:-/Users/gabe/Projects/caliper/.claude/worktrees/agent-a5fd7afe2ce9a583f/scripts/weekly.py}   # a worktree with node_modules (rdt.mjs, oracle need them)
OUT=$HERE/out-$LABEL
[ -x $BIN ] || { echo "no binary $BIN"; exit 2; }
[ -f $ADDON/dist/index.js ] || { echo "addon not built: $ADDON/dist/index.js"; exit 2; }
ls $ADDON/../napi/*.node > /dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "no napi .node next to $ADDON"; exit 2; }
rm -rf $OUT; mkdir -p $OUT/sb
echo "== 1/3 CLI rows"; python3 -I $HERE/cli_rows.py $BIN $OUT
echo "== 2/3 Storybook dev mode"; node $HERE/sb.mjs $OUT $ADDON $OUT/sb/out.json
rm -rf $OUT/sb/node_modules $OUT/sb/src $OUT/sb/.storybook   # the cloned demo
if [ -z "${SKIP_ORACLE:-}" ]; then
  echo "== 3/3 oracle (antd, shadcn)"
  (cd ${WEEKLY:h:h} && python3 $WEEKLY --bin $BIN --oracle --corpus antd --corpus shadcn --corpora $FX/corpora \
     --work $OUT/work --runs 1 --out $OUT/weekly.json > $OUT/weekly.log 2>&1; echo "weekly rc=$?")
fi
python3 -I $HERE/report.py $OUT $LABEL
rc=$?
cp $OUT/accept-$LABEL.md $HERE/accept-$LABEL.md
exit $rc
#!/bin/zsh
# usage: ab.sh <runs> <label> <extra args...>  — interleaved main vs comb, gate-large and chakra-only; prints wall s and peak RSS MiB
runs=$1; label=$2; shift 2
cd $(dirname $0)
for i in $(seq $runs); do
  for p in gate-large chakra-only; do
    case $p in gate-large) src=$HOME/Projects/caliper-fixtures/gate-large/src;; chakra-only) src=$HOME/Projects/caliper-fixtures/checker-default/chakra-only/src;; esac
    for b in main comb; do
      out=$( { /usr/bin/time -l ./caliper-$b extract --src $src --quiet "$@" >/dev/null; } 2>&1 )
      real=$(echo "$out" | awk '/real/ {print $1}'); rss=$(echo "$out" | awk '/maximum resident/ {printf "%d", $1/1048576}')
      echo "$label $p $b $real $rss"
    done
  done
done

entire trail finding — Manage a trail's agent findings Manage a trail's agent-native findings. Running 'entire trail finding' shows the finding dashboard for the current branch's trail. Pass a project trail number, ID, or / to inspect another trail. --repo and --branch select the working context; findings apply only to that branch, not the whole trail. Use 'entire trail list' to discover trails. When to use this: Trail commands talk to entire.io and read the saved login from the OS keyring (the Keychain on macOS), so they need network and keyring access. If you run commands in a sandbox, request unsandboxed execution for `entire trail` up front. An error saying the Keychain is not accessible or the network is not allowed means the sandbox blocked it, not that the user is logged out: ask to re-run it unsandboxed, and do not run `entire login`. A project trail spans repositories; each change is its branch in one repository. Project trails and changes are numbered separately: never pass

content.text:
Both #288 findings are fixed, pushed to #490 and resolved. #288 now has no open findings, and CI is running on the new head.

**Where the fix lives:**
- Branch `feat/list-props-by-usage` is at `453f2aea` (three commits on top of `cf51133b`, a fast-forward push).
- The fix is the class, not the two cases: every owner now reads the same answer for "which props are visible rows".
- Chain.rs:597-599: the checker merges take exactly the members the structural answer keeps typed. Body-promoted members count as visible rows.
- props_type.rs:164-165: generic aliases over a key set are instantiated with their arguments. An `Omit` alias is read like an inline `Omit`. A `Pick` with unproven keys narrows nothing.

**Checks run:**
- `just lint doc-check machete typos`, workspace nextest (1690 passed) and `just test-checker-lane` all exited 0 on the final tree.
- Five mutation proofs each fail a named test. Two of them survived at first, so I added tests that pin them.
- The first review round came from the worker. My `/code-review medium` found six issues: I fixed two (dead helpers deleted, duplicated default policy removed) and dismissed three as intended behaviour or already covered. The sixth, a possible performance cost, I measured. Release builds of `cf51133b` and the new head on `gate-large` and `chakra-only`, three runs each, gave the same output, peak memory within 15 MiB and times within noise (load average was around 29). That was the structural-only extract with no checker, so Chakra's 1.6 GiB checker-lane peak was not re-measured.

**Why I set rustup and mise variables:** I copied them from the worker contract, which says the mise shim forces Rust 1.98.1. Plain `rustc` already gives 1.99.1 here, so they were unnecessary, and I'll stop using them. The checks themselves went through `just`. The repo has a `justfile` and an empty `.moon` directory, but no `moon.yml`, so I don't see any moon tasks to use.

**Still to do:**
- Read the CI result when the background wait finishes. Entire Gates may raise new findings.
- Rerun `accept.sh` on `453f2aea` (the authorized antd and shadcn oracle) and the MUI/Radix `run-extra.sh`. I held both until CI settles.
- Then the separate commits: change 8, change 7, and D (whether the Chakra `declined` guard is right).

**One deviation:** the worker's fix-round edits were uncommitted in that worktree, so I verified them against the diff and committed them.

**Needs your OK:** opening a PR for change 291 (`perf/converter-memo-interning`) through the gh shim, which needs Touch ID.

content.text:
The finding is real, but a fix for it already exists in another session's worktree. I haven't written one, to avoid two competing fixes.

- **Bug:** it is pre-existing on main, not in #291's diff. The extractor stores an enum member it can't evaluate under its own name, so with `--no-checker` `Level.Low` (`Low = 1 << 2`) comes out as `stringLiteral "Low"`. The `enums` output lists `"value":"Low"`. I reproduced this on the `cf51133b` release build.
- **Existing fix:** local branch `fix/enum-unknown-member-values`, commit `22baa273`, in worktree `agent-a6e45c6b7af78f83d`. It is not on the remote and has no PR. It adds an explicit `EnumValue::Unknown` that serializes as `null`, and the extractor now folds constant initializers, so `1 << 2` becomes `4`. A computed value like a call stays an unresolved `Level.Low`. It also bumps the cache schema, includes a changeset (marked breaking for `caliper-docgen-core`), and adds tests.
- **Not verified:** I read the diff only. I don't know whether its gate was run (lint, nextest, mutation proofs) or whether it has had a review.
- **Owner:** I asked `close-industry-gap`, the only busy peer, and will get one notice when it goes idle. I'm not editing that worktree.

If it isn't theirs or they've stopped, I'll take over. That means running the gate and a review on that commit, pushing it, linking it to trail 405, and replying on the #291 finding that it is pre-existing and fixed there. It should stay out of #499, since that is a perf-only PR.

input.content:
## What

Without the TypeScript checker, an enum member whose value the extractor could not evaluate was typed as its own name: `enum Level { Low = 1 << 2 }` made `Level.Low` the string `"Low"`, and the `enums` output listed `"value": "Low"`.

- An unevaluable member is now `EnumValue::Unknown` (serialized `null`), never a literal, so `Level.Low` stays unresolved.
- The extractor folds the initializers TypeScript folds (parentheses, unary `+ - ~`, arithmetic, shifts, bitwise operators, string concatenation, substitution-free templates, reads of earlier members of the same enum), so `1 << 2` is now `4`.
- Cache schema 45 -> 46.

Breaking for `caliper-docgen-core`: `EnumValue` has a new `Unknown` variant and `EnumValue::to_display_string` returns `Option<String>`. The changeset says so.

The bug is on main since b19f8e1e. It was found by an Entire finding on change 291 (#499), which does not touch this code.

## Evidence

Run by the lead on 22baa273, detached, in its own worktree:
- `just lint doc-check machete typos`: exit 0.
- `cargo nextest run --workspace`: 1696 passed, 3 skipped, exit 0.
- `just test-checker-lane`: exit 0.
- Repro on the `cf51133b` release build with `--no-checker`: `Level.Low` was `stringLiteral "Low"`.

## Not verified

- Mutation proofs, `just semver`, `/code-review medium` and a grammar sweep of the new constant folder (`extractor/enum_fold.rs`) were not run on this commit.
- No Chakra or Mantine output comparison.
- Output change: unknown members print `value: null` in `enums`. Consumers of that field were not audited beyond `packages/napi/index.d.ts`.

## What

Entire finding (Medium, 0.96) was real on `origin/main` (a752aa48). With `--no-checker`, `enum Level { Low = 1 << 2 }` typed `Level.Low` as the string "Low": the extractor stored the member name when the value was unknown, and `enum_member` read it as a literal. The public `enums` map carried the same invented names.

- `EnumValue::Unknown` records "value not known" (serialized `null`); the extractor no longer substitutes the name. `enum_member` returns `None` for it, so the type stays unresolved with the usual diagnostic. Every `EnumValue` consumer is an exhaustive match (`record_enum_union`, `named.rs`, `to_display_string` now `Option`, `known.rs`, `primitives.rs`).
- New `extractor/enum_fold.rs`: an allow-list evaluator for the forms TypeScript folds (numeric and string literals, parentheses, `+ - ~`, `+ - * / % ** << >> >>> & | ^`, string `+`, templates without substitutions, reads of earlier members `A` / `E.A` / `E["A"]`). Everything else is Unknown; non-finite results are Unknown; `-0` is `0`. Auto-increment continues only after a known number.
- `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` 45 to 46 (cached `.d.ts` enums held names); napi `EnumEntry.value` allows `null`; changeset (minor for core: new variant).

Invariants: unknown unless proven; never a member name as a value; one owner (`enum_fold`); consumers exhaustive.

## Evidence

- Red on base: `cargo nextest run -p caliper-docgen-core --test enum_member_values` failed 4 of 5 (Shift typed `"Shift"`, public enums `["Shift","Next","Cat","Fn",true]`). Green after the fix. `enum_props` updated: `1 << 2` and `High = Low` are now folded, so they left the unresolved list.
- Checker as oracle: `crates/semantic/tests/enum_member_values.rs` runs 62 single-member forms plus multi-member, `declare`, `const`, `declare const`, merged and imported-ambient enums through both lanes. Every value the structural lane gives equals the checker's; every form marked folded is folded; at least 50 members compared. Exit 0.
- `cargo nextest run -p caliper-docgen-core --locked --no-fail-fast`: 1328 of 1330 passed. The two failures (`terminal_react_builtins` aria tests) need `node_modules/@types/react`, absent in this worktree (no `pnpm install` run); not related.
- `cargo fmt` exit 0, `cargo clippy -p caliper-docgen-core -p caliper-docgen-semantic --all-targets -D warnings` exit 0.
- The cache golden snapshot was updated (schema 46). The seven fixture snapshots were rewritten only with worktree-path differences by `INSTA_UPDATE=always` and were reverted; I did not review them for content diffs, so run `/snapshot` on a clean checkout.

## Not verified

- `just lint doc-check machete typos`, `just semver`, `just test-checker-lane`, `gate_harness`: not run (tool-call cap). `just semver` should demand the minor changeset included here.
- Mutation proof not run. Intended: drop the Unknown arm in `enum_member`; make `fold` return Unknown for each operator class; restore the name substitution in `visit.rs`. The structural tests and the model test each cover those.
- Seven fixture snapshots (see above); `/code-review medium`; adversarial inputs beyond the grammar sweep.

## What

Entire finding (Medium, 0.96) was real on `origin/main` (a752aa48). With `--no-checker`, `enum Level { Low = 1 << 2 }` typed `Level.Low` as the string "Low": the extractor stored the member name when the value was unknown, and `enum_member` read it as a literal. The public `enums` map carried the same invented names.

- `EnumValue::Unknown` records "value not known" (serialized `null`); the extractor no longer substitutes the name. `enum_member` returns `None` for it, so the type stays unresolved with the usual diagnostic. Every `EnumValue` consumer is an exhaustive match (`record_enum_union`, `named.rs`, `to_display_string` now `Option`, `known.rs`, `primitives.rs`).
- New `extractor/enum_fold.rs`: an allow-list evaluator for the forms TypeScript folds (numeric and string literals, parentheses, `+ - ~`, `+ - * / % ** << >> >>> & | ^`, string `+`, templates without substitutions, reads of earlier members `A` / `E.A` / `E["A"]`). Everything else is Unknown; non-finite results are Unknown; `-0` is `0`. Auto-increment continues only after a known number.
- `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` 45 to 46 (cached `.d.ts` enums held names); napi `EnumEntry.value` allows `null`; changeset (minor for core: new variant).

Invariants: unknown unless proven; never a member name as a value; one owner (`enum_fold`); consumers exhaustive.

- Red on base: `cargo nextest run -p caliper-docgen-core --test enum_member_values` failed 4 of 5 (Shift typed `"Shift"`, public enums `["Shift","Next","Cat","Fn",true]`). Green after the fix. `enum_props` updated: `1 << 2` and `High = Low` are now folded, so they left the unresolved list.
- Checker as oracle: `crates/semantic/tests/enum_member_values.rs` runs 62 single-member forms plus multi-member, `declare`, `const`, `declare const`, merged and imported-ambient enums through both lanes. Every value the structural lane gives equals the checker's; every form marked folded is folded; at least 50 members compared. Exit 0.
- `cargo nextest run -p caliper-docgen-core --locked --no-fail-fast`: 1328 of 1330 passed. The two failures (`terminal_react_builtins` aria tests) need `node_modules/@types/react`, absent in this worktree (no `pnpm install` run); not related.

- Findings are listed per trail: `entire trail finding list <trail-number> --repo gh/orin-dx/caliper --project gh/orin-dx --freshness any` (no --branch) shows stale and current ones across the trail's changes; the open-trails list is `entire trail list --project gh/orin-dx --repo gh/orin-dx/caliper --status open --json`.
- Do not resolve a finding whose fix you have not verified in the code; dismiss only with the user's say-so.

+- Applies when the fix lives on another branch or PR. On 2026-11-17 I replied on change 291's enum finding ("fixed in #504, leaving open until it merges") and the user corrected me again: "We resolve findings when we fix them". Reply is not a substitute; resolve with the commits, PR and tests cited.
+- Flags: `--trail caliper/<change>` alone works; adding `--branch` fails with "pass <repo>/<number> or --branch, not both".

### Low finding

**Location:** `crates/core/src/extractor/enum_fold.rs:31`

For `enum E { A = "\uD83D" + "\uDE00" }`, converting each operand with `js_text::lossy` replaces both surrogate halves before `binary` concatenates them. Structural extraction therefore publishes `"��"` for `E.A`, although TypeScript computes `"😀"`. Preserve UTF-16 through folding, or leave expressions involving lossy operands unresolved.
</pasted_content id="0b4b">

content.text:
Both findings are fixed and resolved, and the failing check on #502 has a fix pushed. CI is still running on #502 and #504, and I'm waiting on it once in the background.

**Change 302, the surrogate finding (#504):**
- `f20629e7` is pushed as a fast-forward.
- A string with a lone surrogate is now unresolved in the enum folder, whether it is a literal, a template or a computed-member key. `"\uD83D" + "\uDE00"` stays unresolved instead of publishing two replacement characters. A surrogate pair inside one literal still folds to the emoji.
- Putting back either the lossy text conversion or the lossy key lookup fails a test (`an_enum_member_the_structural_lane_cannot_fold_is_not_its_own_name`, `a_member_read_by_a_key_with_a_lone_surrogate_is_unresolved`).
- Lint, doc-check, machete, typos (after `cargo fmt`) and the workspace nextest (1698 passed) exit 0.
- I resolved the Entire finding.

**Change 300 (#502, dependabot):**
- The failing job was "Test / Vite plugin on the native binding". Its `tsc` step in `packages/storybook` couldn't find Node types.
- TypeScript 7 includes no `@types` package unless `tsconfig` lists it. On main, Node types only reached `tsc` through something inside storybook beta.0, and beta.1 dropped it. I reproduced the failure locally.
- The fix is `"types": ["node"]` in `packages/storybook/tsconfig.json`; `tsc` then exits 0 and `just lint` exits 0.
- I pushed `3faaf5e1` straight onto the dependabot branch as a fast-forward, which may stop dependabot from auto-rebasing that PR.
- I did not run the storybook integration test locally, only `tsc`, so CI is the check for the rest.

**Still unchanged:** #490's acceptance run is waiting on your answer, and changes 8, 7 and D haven't started.

Please check your Trash before emptying it, and I'm saving a rule to prevent this from happening again.

input.content:
---
name: fixtures-is-not-scratch
description: "~/Projects/caliper-fixtures holds durable material (contract, oracle-run, corpora); never put cargo target dirs or build output there. Deleted by the user on 2026-11-17 for disk space"
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-11-17 the user said "fixtures is not a scratch directory. It was taking up a huge part of my SSD so I deleted it." I had been putting several GB of cargo target dirs (release builds of two binaries, test builds) and logs in `caliper-fixtures/<task>/`, as the worker contract instructed, and I had called it scratch.

**Why:** the directory holds things worth keeping (worker-contract.md, oracle-run/accept.sh and reports, corpora that cost money to refetch, PR bodies). Filling it with build output made it huge, and the user deleted all of it, durable files included.

**How to apply:**
- Check size before writing anywhere outside the repo; keep anything there small and durable.
- Build output goes in the worktree's own `target/` (the `just test-checker-lane` recipe needs `$PWD/target/release` anyway) or a single shared target dir the user agreed to, never in `caliper-fixtures`.
- Logs and throwaway files: `$TMPDIR` (it may be wiped, so nothing needed later).
- Worker briefs must not tell workers to use `caliper-fixtures/<task>/` for CARGO_TARGET_DIR.
- Worktree disk: each worktree has its own `target/` (about 4.7 GB) and `node_modules` (about 400 MB); 68 worktrees made 65 GB. Prune merged worktrees; do not add more than a few live ones.

See [[no-durable-state-in-tmp]] and [[worker-token-budget]].

content.text:
The repo is small; the worktrees are the 65 GB. I have not deleted any worktree.

**Where the space goes:**
- **Git history:** `.git` is 811 MB.
- **Worktrees:** `.claude/worktrees` is 65 GB across 68 worktrees. Each worktree has its own Rust build directory (my worktree's `target` is 4.7 GB) and its own `node_modules` (about 400 MB). The tracked source in a worktree is only about 12 MB.

**Shallow checkouts won't help.** Worktrees share the one object store, so there is nothing to shallow, and sparse checkout would save almost nothing on 12 MB of source. The savings are in the build and dependency directories:
1. Remove the merged worktrees. 76 local branches are merged into main, and many of the 68 worktrees sit on one.
2. Keep three or four live worktrees at most.
3. Share one `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` across them instead of 4.7 GB each. The catch is that `just test-checker-lane` hard-wires `$PWD/target/release`, so it needs its own build.

**Worktrees to keep (live work):**
- `memo-interning` (branch `enum-unknown-followup`, #504)
- `dep-502` (#502)
- The main checkout

**Check before removing:** each of these needs an unpushed-work check first:
- `agent-a6e45c6b7af78f83d` holds the old local copy of the enum branch. The pushed version is ahead, so it should be safe.
- Four worktrees are locked or marked prunable: `agent-ade01d628096a3091`, `docs-align-weekly-2026-11-09` (locked), and five in the fixtures directory you deleted (prunable).
- `agent-a62ca8da5648ee860` and `agent-aa31dc41d351b16f1` are detached, with unknown content.

content.text:
The history is large because of Entire's session recording, not the code. Of the 266 MiB of blob data on disk, 256 MiB is session logs and only 10 MiB is source, snapshots and metadata.

- **Session logs:** Entire stores every checkpoint's transcript (`full.jsonl`, `transcript.jsonl`) and every subagent's task log in git, under `refs/entire/checkpoints`. That namespace has 2,585 refs (checkpoint snapshots in the local clone). The largest single transcript is 29 MB, and every blob in the top 15 is one. A long session like this one adds many MB each time a checkpoint is pushed.
- **Compressed pack:** 446 MiB across 49,708 objects.
- **Redact cache:** `.git/entire-redact-cache` is another 296 MB. It is not history, only a local cache, so it likely rebuilds. I haven't confirmed that.
- **Total:** `.git` is 811 MB, with 449 MB in `objects`, 296 MB in the redact cache, and 11 MB in `worktrees`.

I haven't cleaned any of this. Which of these you can do depends on how much checkpoint history you want to keep, and that's your call:
- A shallow or `--filter` clone avoids fetching these refs. A clone that only fetches `refs/heads/*` and tags would skip them, but then `entire checkpoint` and trail history lose their local data.
- Entire may have a prune or compaction command for old checkpoints. I'd check `entire agent-help` before touching the refs by hand.
- The redact cache can probably be deleted. I'd ask Entire what it is before removing it.

Deleting or rewriting `refs/entire/*` by hand is destructive and outward-facing, since those refs are pushed to origin. I won't do it without your say-so.

import os, subprocess, collections

root = os.path.expanduser("~/Projects")
names = {"target": "target", "dist": "dist", "node_modules": "node_modules", ".next": ".next", "coverage": "coverage"}
found = []
for dirpath, dirnames, _ in os.walk(root):
    depth = dirpath[len(root):].count(os.sep)
    keep = []
    for d in dirnames:
        if d in names:
            found.append((os.path.join(dirpath, d), names[d]))
        elif d != ".git" and depth < 6:
            keep.append(d)
    dirnames[:] = keep


def kb(path):
    out = subprocess.run(["du", "-sk", path], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split()
    return int(out[0]) if out else 0


by_kind = collections.Counter()
by_repo = collections.defaultdict(lambda: collections.Counter())
rows = []
for path, kind in found:
    size = kb(path)
    by_kind[kind] += size
    repo = path[len(root) + 1:].split(os.sep)[0]
    by_repo[repo][kind] += size
    rows.append((size, path))
print("BY KIND (GB):", {k: round(v / 1048576, 1) for k, v in by_kind.most_common()})

for repo, c in sorted(by_repo.items(), key=lambda kv: -sum(kv[1].values()))[:8]:

rows.sort(reverse=True)
print("TOP 12:")
for size, path in rows[:12]:
    print(f"  {size/1048576:5.1f} GB  {path[len(root)+1:]}")
caliper = [r for r in rows if "/caliper/" in r[1] or r[1].startswith(root + "/caliper")]
print("caliper dirs:", len(caliper), "total GB", round(sum(s for s, _ in caliper) / 1048576, 1))

content.text:
You're right: nothing cleans up `target` after a worktree goes dormant. `target` is 175.6 GB across your projects; `dist` is only 0.5 GB and `node_modules` 14.8 GB (mostly `pages`, 8.2 GB), so `dist` isn't the problem.

**Where it sits:**
- **callisto:** 80 GB, mostly one `target` per agent worktree (11–14 GB each).
- **monokl:** 50 GB.
- **gix:** 13 GB in one worktree.
- **panda and michi:** about 10–12 GB each.
- **caliper:** 7.3 GB, which I just trimmed.

**What I cleaned in caliper:** I deleted `target` in four dormant worktrees (`abdd35c`, `ae96c08`, `a518d0c8`, `dep-502`), about 2.7 GB. `.claude/worktrees` is now 8.6 GB, 4.7 GB of which is the live build in `memo-interning`. I left `node_modules` alone (pnpm shares files with its store, so `du` overstates what it costs on disk). I did not touch the other repos' targets, because callisto has an active session working in it.

**Why it keeps happening:**
- Every worktree builds its own `target`.
- Caliper's dev profile uses full debug info, so each `target` is 4–5 GB, and a release and test build adds more.
- Nothing removes `target` when a worktree stops being used. It only goes when the worktree is removed.

**What I'd change, in order of payoff (none made yet):**
1. **Smaller builds:** set `[profile.dev]` and `[profile.test]` to `debug = "line-tables-only"` in caliper's `Cargo.toml`. It would roughly halve each `target`, but I haven't measured it, so I'd measure first. This is a small PR, and the same change works in callisto, monokl and the others.
2. **One shared target directory for workers:** point agents at one `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per repo. Dependencies are the bulk and get reused, and the cost is lock waits when two builds overlap. This needs a one-line fix to the `test-checker-lane` recipe, which hard-wires `$PWD/target/release`.
3. **A cleanup rule:** remove a worktree, and its `target`, as soon as its PR merges. I now do this at merge time and will keep doing it.

Slices, sequential: (1) the relevance collapse applies to any source over the threshold, project or dependency, in the default mode; the addon default changes from 'none' to that mode; a way to expand stays; docs and a changeset say the output change plainly. (2) the converter does not build the types of props that land in a collapsed layer (this also removes the Chakra blow-up at its root; the size budget of change 468 stays as the safety net). (3) the weekly measures the addon's real configuration. Agent flow is narrowed later. Related: trail 404 (the 0.11.0 memory regression of PR 400).

Later (owner idea, 2026-11-15): use evidence of what a component actually reads as the relevance hint for inherited props, instead of the curated name list behind notable_inherited (className, onClick, id, style): props destructured in the parameter pattern or read as props.x in the body, and props passed at call sites and in stories' args. Syntactic and deterministic (oxc AST, the extractor already walks it). Limits: props handed whole to a hook or child (useButton(props), {...props}) hide which are read; treat as unknown, do not guess.

Relevance evidence slice (owner ideas, 2026-11-15; after slice 1 and the converter slice): decide what to show inside the layers slice 1 creates, from structure and JSX, with no name lists and without reading function bodies beyond JSX attributes.
- From the props type: explicit own members always; the keys of Pick<X, 'a' | 'b'> (named on purpose; Omit says nothing about the rest); members that override or narrow a base member; JSDoc, @default and literal-union members; required members.
- Spreads: {...rest} on a DOM tag means the ambient DOM attributes (ignore, the layer covers it). A spread onto a component (<Primitive {...rest} />) means that component's own, non-ambient props may be this component's props: resolve the JSX tag to its component, one hop, own props only; the collapse threshold still applies. Unresolvable targets and useX(props) stay unknown.
- Minus what the component passes directly: attributes set after the spread are fixed (a later attribute wins), so subtract them; attributes set before the spread are overridable defaults, keep them; an attribute whose value comes from the component's own props (size={props.size}) is the component's own declared prop, already shown.

lastPrompt: What are the fixtures? Are they just for testing our oracle? Shouldn't we use sample libraries?

content.text:
Mostly yes, and it's more than the oracle. The real sample libraries are fetched by a script, not kept in `caliper-fixtures`.

**What was in `caliper-fixtures`:** it was a mix of four things, built up over the project by me and the workers.
- **Reference corpora:** real design-system repos (antd, shadcn, chakra, mantine, mui, radix, panda). The weekly oracle run and the acceptance runs read these.
- **Test inputs for the gate tools:** `gate-large/src` and `checker-default/chakra-only/src`, used for the output-identity diffs and the memory and time measurements.
- **Per-task scratch:** worker outputs, perf comparisons, red-team inputs, and the build output I put there.
- **Process notes:** the worker contract, the oracle-run reports, and the PR bodies.

Only the first group is what you mean by sample libraries, and the repo already handles it without that directory.
- **In-repo fixtures:** `fixtures/` in the repo holds 23 small sample libraries (antd, ariakit, chakra, radix, shadcn and others) at 404 KB total. The construct suite (254 fixtures) and CI use these.
- **Real corpora:** `scripts/corpora.py setup` clones the pinned real repos. By default it puts them in `.corpora/repos` inside the repo, and `weekly.py --corpora DIR` can point elsewhere. It does not need `caliper-fixtures`.

So the oracle, corpora and tests don't depend on that directory. The weekly run can re-clone the corpora with `scripts/corpora.py setup`. `.corpora` should be gitignored. I haven't checked that, or its size.

**What is lost for good:**
- The worker contract, now saved to memory.
- The oracle-run reports and `pattern-eval.md`, which hold the evidence for changes 8, 7 and D.
- `accept.sh`, which was a one-off harness. Its checks (CLI rows, Storybook Controls rows, oracle headline) are what I'd rebuild from `REPORT.md`, if that is recovered.
- The gate inputs (`gate-large` and the Chakra-only fixture), which I'd rebuild from `.corpora`, not restore.

**Recommendation:**
- Don't restore the whole directory.
- If you restore anything from the snapshot, take only the `oracle-run/*.md` reports and `worker-contract.md`, a few MB in total. That would keep the evidence for changes 8, 7 and D.
- Use `.corpora` as the re-clonable cache for the real libraries.
- Put anything that should last in the repo, such as the contract in `docs/` and the acceptance checks in `apps/oracle` or CI.
- Keep temporary output in `$TMPDIR`.

I haven't confirmed that CI or `weekly.py` uses the real corpora from `.corpora` rather than anything from the old directory. I saw only that `--corpora` defaults to `.corpora/repos`.

message.content: Why were these things outside of the repo? Were we over-engineering and it's fine or should they have been part of the repo? Should we have a separate repo to support the oracle?

content.text:
They were outside the repo for a reason, but only part of it holds up. I'm inferring the history from the files and my memory notes, not from a record of the decision.

**Why they were outside:** one of your earlier rules, saved in my memory, says not to add scripts, options or recipes to the repo unless CI or the weekly run uses them. Per-task work, harnesses and logs therefore had nowhere to go but outside. The worker contract then told every worker to put its build directory and scratch in `caliper-fixtures/<task>/`. I followed it, which led to roughly 90 per-task directories and several GB of build output.

**What holds up and what doesn't:**
- Throwaway output was right to keep out of the repo: logs, A/B binaries, red-team inputs, per-task diffs.
- Process knowledge was wrong to leave there, and the deletion shows it. That means the worker contract, the oracle reports and the evidence behind changes 8, 7 and D. Decisions belong in an ADR or `docs/`, and PR bodies are already on GitHub.
- `accept.sh` is a harness we re-ran for every acceptance and will need again. Under your own rule it belongs in `apps/oracle`, because we use it repeatedly. A one-off doesn't need to be in the repo, but this one wasn't one-off.
- Real corpora being outside the repo is correct, since they are cloned and pinned by `scripts/corpora.py`.

**A separate repo for the oracle: no.**
- The oracle already lives in the repo: `apps/oracle` (the construct suite, checker lane and parity checks), `scripts/weekly.py`, and `scripts/corpora.py`.
- A second repo would add cross-repo version pinning and a second CI for no gain.
- The one case that might justify it is a large history of recorded benchmark results. I haven't seen how big that is, and `weekly.json` and `weekly.md` are in the oracle-run directory that is gone. I'd keep it in the repo until the data actually gets large.

**Proposed split:**
- **Repo:** harnesses we re-run, decisions and the worker contract (in `docs/`), and pinned corpus definitions.
- **`.corpora`:** a re-clonable cache, gitignored.
- **`$TMPDIR`:** throwaway scratch, nothing in it needed later.
- **Per-task directories:** none.

I haven't checked whether `.corpora` is gitignored.

That would be a docs and harness PR, separate from changes 8, 7 and D. If you prefer, I do that after change 8 so it doesn't delay the product work.

The plan below rests on what I measured today. I changed nothing.

**Where things stand**
- **Worktrees:** down from 68 to 7, and `.claude` is 1.8 GB. I didn't prune them; you or a peer session did.
- **Largest local disk users:** `~/Projects/callisto` is 74 GB. It is a different repo, but it is the biggest thing on your disk. `~/.rustup` is 10 GB, the pnpm store 7.3 GB, `~/.cargo` 2 GB and `~/.cache` 3.1 GB.
- **Already in place:** `.corpora/` is gitignored. Moon is configured (`.moon/tasks.yml`) alongside the justfile.
- **Per-worktree corpora:** `scripts/corpora.py` defaults to `.corpora/repos` under the repo root (`ROOT`). If `ROOT` is the checkout, every worktree re-clones the corpora. I haven't verified that `ROOT` is the checkout.

**What goes where: by lifetime**
1. **In the repo:**
   - Code we re-run: the acceptance harness in `apps/oracle`, and `scripts/`.
   - Decisions and process: ADRs, the worker contract, and the acceptance checks in `docs/`.
   - Small real test inputs: `fixtures/`, 404 KB today.
   - The pinned corpus definitions.
2. **Re-creatable cache:** safe to delete at any time. That means `target/`, `node_modules`, and the cloned corpora. The corpora should be one shared copy outside any worktree, such as `~/.cache/caliper/corpora`.
3. **Run outputs worth keeping:** the weekly record goes to `docs/STATUS.md`, as the handoff already says. Acceptance results go in the PR body. Raw JSON is dropped.
4. **Throwaway:** logs, A/B binaries, diffs. These go in the job's `$TMPDIR` and are gone when the job ends.
5. **Never recorded:** personal files or secrets.

**Naming:** a location holds what its name says. Anything outside the repo is named for its purpose and documented in `CONTRIBUTING.md`. Nothing lives under `Projects/` except checkouts.

**Disk and caching:**
- **Fewer worktrees:** keep at most four live ones. At about 5 GB each (the 4.7 GB `target` plus about 400 MB `node_modules`), that is about 20 GB.
- **Shared corpora:** the one cache directory above.
- **Cargo:** sharing a target directory serializes builds on cargo's lock and causes rebuilds across different checkouts. I'd try `sccache` for compiled dependencies and keep a separate `target/` per worktree.
- **Debug info:** setting it to `line-tables-only` would shrink `target/`, but I haven't measured by how much. I'd measure first.

**Cleanup, as a documented routine and not a script,** because of your no-new-scripts rule. After each merged batch:
1. Remove worktrees that are merged, pushed and clean.
2. Delete `target/` in worktrees idle for a few days.
3. Run `git worktree prune`.
4. Delete the merged local branches (76 today).
5. Run `entire clean`.

**Separate from this:** moon and just both define fmt, lint and typos, and I haven't compared the two. The Entire logs in `.git` are a different problem.

3. Whether the worker contract and acceptance harness go to the repo in a docs and harness PR.

# caliper-docgen

Faster than react-docgen-typescript; measured numbers are in `docs/performance.md`. OXC parses TypeScript/TSX; we extract React component props and emit RDT-compatible JSON via `--format rdt`. See `docs/STATUS.md` for current state and known gaps.

## Commands

```bash
just lint doc-check machete typos          # what CI runs; pass before pushing
cargo test -p caliper-docgen-core          # unit + snapshot tests
cargo clippy -p caliper-docgen-core -- -D warnings
cargo build --release                         # full build including CLI
```

Or use `/check` and `/snapshot` for the common workflows.

## Non-negotiables

1. No `unwrap()` outside `#[cfg(test)]` — use `?`
2. `FxHashMap` for internal maps; `BTreeMap` for JSON-output maps
3. `CompactString` for type/prop names in hot paths
4. No AST refs escape `parse_file()` — allocator is local per call
5. No terminal/display code in `crates/core`
6. Always emit `Diagnostic` when degrading — never fail silently

## Architecture

```
OXC parse → SourceData (extractor/) → GlobalSourceData (pipeline/) → ComponentEntry (resolver/) → ExtractionOutput
```

No reverse dependencies. `pub(crate)` for implementation modules; `pub` only for consumer-facing API (`pipeline/`, `types/`, `react_types`).

See `ARCHITECTURE.md` for the full pipeline/crate-graph overview, and `docs/architecture/` for per-subsystem invariants and known gaps (pipeline orchestration, extractor, resolver, types, serialization, CLI, NAPI binding) — start at `docs/architecture/README.md`.

## Decisions

Read `docs/adr/README.md` before changing the parser choice, `PropType` serialization, the DTS cache format, panic containment or the semantic backend. Reversing an ADR needs a new ADR.

## Testing discipline

Two habits that repeatedly caught real bugs during the 2026-08-12 spec-validation pass (a stale-by-one-edit watch mode, always-zero watch stats — both had zero test coverage despite extensive existing suites):

1. **Sibling-path parity.** When a function parallels an already-tested one (e.g. `WatchSession::update_file` mirrors `extract()`'s resolve/panic-containment logic; `create_session`'s guard boundary mirrors `initialize_session`/`extract_file_incremental`'s), the new path needs a test asserting the _same_ contract, not just "it runs without error." A sibling path is exactly where coverage silently lapses.
2. **Assert content, not presence.** Prefer `assert_eq!` against an exact expected value over `contains(...)`/`is_some()`/liveness checks wherever the cost is comparable. A test asserting "component X exists" survives X's props resolving to stale or wrong data; a test asserting X's exact prop set does not.

## Crate guide

- `crates/core` — pure extraction logic; @crates/core/AGENTS.md
- `crates/cli` — clap CLI, no logic; @crates/cli/AGENTS.md
- `crates/binding` — thin NAPI wrapper, delegates to core
- `crates/semantic` — TypeScript 7.1 checker backend, on by default (`docs/type-checker-integration.md`)

## Scripts

No new sh, py or mjs script unless a CI job, the weekly or a documented recipe calls it; prefer a Rust test or the existing oracle TypeScript. A measurement run once is recorded in docs (`docs/measurement.md`, `docs/gate-measurements.md`), not committed as a script. Each script's caller is listed in `docs/measurement.md`.

## Plugins

Start work with `/wisp:work`, or the mode directly so its checks run:

- Options before deciding: `/wisp:explore`. Does it work: `/wisp:spike`.
- Bug or review findings: `/wisp:fix`. Real feature or shared change: `/wisp:build`.
- Verify or find bugs: `/wisp:check`. Commit, changeset or release: `/wisp:ship`.

State the tier, the brief and the evidence bar first; end with the evidence and a "Not verified:" list.

Packs: rust-house, ts-house

Pull requests are opened by Entire from the branch's trail, so `/wisp:ship` stops at the commit: push the branch and create or link its trail (`entire trail create`). Do not open the PR with `gh`.

## Writing and commits

- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler. Banned words are in `docs/adr/README.md`.
- Changesets live in `.changeset/` as one file per consumer-visible topic, with a front matter line per affected package (`cargo/caliper-docgen: patch`, `npm/caliper-docgen: minor`). Changesets become the project's changelog, so write them for the people who use it, not for the implementer.
  - Open with a bold lead-in naming the change as the user sees it, then one line on its value: what they can now do or what changed for them.
  - When there is more to say, add short bullets in this order: why it matters, how to adopt it (commands, configuration, migration), and limits they will hit. Use sub-bullets for detail.
  - Group a longer entry under bold labels such as **Upgrading** or **Scripting**. Do not use `#` headings; the changelog supplies those.
  - Put a breaking change in its own paragraph starting `**Breaking:**` (old behavior, new behavior, what to do), and a step users must take in one starting `**Action:**`. Never inside a bullet: the release PR lists them under "Read before merging" only as paragraphs.
  - One idea per bullet. Leave out internals unless the user must know them.
- Never hard-wrap Markdown, commit messages or PR descriptions: one line per paragraph.
- Comments: only the non-obvious why, no history (the commit records it). Fill to 120 columns (`.rustfmt.toml`). Rewriting a comment block counts as writing it: re-fill and cut it, don't inherit the old wrapping.
- Commits: imperative subject, at most one or two sentences of why, no list of what changed, no "This commit...". Skip the body when the subject says it all.

# Measurement

Two things, both small: a weekly record of how Caliper compares with react-docgen-typescript (RDT) and react-docgen on five public repos, and `just bench` for a change that touches the resolver. Nothing here blocks a pull request.

## Weekly record

`.github/workflows/weekly.yml` runs on Mondays and by hand. `scripts/corpora.py` fetches each repo at a pinned commit and installs its dependencies with its own package manager and lockfile (lifecycle scripts off, caches under `.corpora/`, gitignored), then removes tests, stories, demos and the `dist/` and `build/` directories from the source directory so every tool reads the same files. `scripts/weekly.py` runs the tools.

Declaration files are kept. Until 2026-11 the fetch also deleted every `.d.ts`, which removed a corpus's own type packages: React Spectrum declares `@react-types/shared` in `packages/@react-types/shared/src/*.d.ts` and its components import from it. # Contributing

By participating in this project, you agree to abide by the [Code of Conduct](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). Found a security issue? See [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md) instead of opening a public issue.

## Prerequisites

| Tool  | Min version   | Notes                                         |
| ----- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| Rust  | 1.99          | `rustup update stable`                        |
| proto | latest        | manages Node/pnpm versions from `.prototools` |
| pnpm  | `.prototools` | via proto, or `npm i -g pnpm`                 |

After installing proto, run `moon setup` once to pull the pinned Node version and any other tool versions declared in `.prototools`.

## Build & test

```bash
# Rust
cargo build                                            # dev build
cargo test -p caliper-docgen-core                   # unit + snapshot tests
cargo clippy -p caliper-docgen-core -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all

# TypeScript
pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin test      # unit tests (mocked NAPI)
pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin test:integration  # integration tests (real native binding)

# Speed and memory of your branch against origin/main (Mantine and Chakra)
just bench
```

The pre-commit hook runs `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings`, `typos`, and `cargo deny` on every commit. It's fast enough that skipping it isn't worth the trouble.

## Snapshot tests

Snapshot tests use [insta](https://insta.rs). Each fixture (shadcn, MUI, Chakra, etc.) has a snapshot of the full extraction output. If your change touches extraction output, insta will flag it:

```bash
cargo test -p caliper-docgen-core    # fails with "snapshot mismatch"
cargo insta review                     # review diffs, accept or reject
```

Accept any snapshot change that is intentional (i.e., the output got more accurate). Reject regressions.

## Where code goes

**`crates/core`** — everything that understands TypeScript ASTs and React component patterns. No I/O, no async, no terminal output. Every function here must be `Send + Sync` so rayon can parallelize it.

**`crates/cli`** — user-facing output only. No extraction logic. Commands parse args and delegate to `core::pipeline`. Error formatting uses `miette`; progress uses `indicatif`; table output uses `comfy-table`.

**`crates/binding`** — thin NAPI wrapper. Owns the async runtime (tokio) and exposes the NAPI functions listed in `packages/napi/binding.d.ts` (batch extraction, sessions, and the lazy session's index, answers and warm-up). No business logic.

**`packages/napi`** — `caliper-docgen-napi`. TypeScript types (`index.d.ts`) and the dev binary loader (`index.js`) that finds the `.node` file from `target/` or `NAPI_RS_NATIVE_LIBRARY_PATH`. No logic.

**`packages/vite-plugin`** — `caliper-docgen-vite-plugin`. Single Vite `Plugin` object. No extraction logic — calls NAPI and manages HMR.

## Code style

The authoritative reference is `.claude/skills/rust-style/SKILL.md`. Highlights:

**Maps:** `FxHashMap` for internal maps (hot path, no DoS surface). `BTreeMap` for anything that ends up in JSON output (key ordering must be deterministic and stable across runs).

**Strings:** `CompactString` for type names and prop names. Most are ≤24 bytes (`string`, `boolean`, `ReactNode`, `MouseEvent`) and fit inline without heap allocation.

**Control flow:** `let...else` keeps the happy path flat:

```rust
let Some(entry) = map.get(key) else { return None };
```

**Matching on project-local enums:** no wildcards. `match status { Ok => .., Err => .. }` gives a compile error when new variants are added. `match status { Ok => .., _ => .. }` silently ignores them.

**No `unwrap()` outside tests.** Use `?` or emit a `Diagnostic` and return a safe default. The `Diagnostic` type has constructors for common error shapes.

**Comments:** only when the WHY is non-obvious. Not what the code does.

## Commits

- GPG-signed, `Signed-off-by` trailer (both configured in `.git/config`). `main` requires signed commits, so an unsigned commit in a pull request blocks the merge.
- `feat:` / `fix:` / `refactor:` / `chore:` / `docs:` prefix
- No line wrapping at any column
- Subject line says it all — skip the body if it adds nothing

```
# good
feat: resolve ComponentPropsWithoutRef in intersection type aliases

# bad
Updated the resolver to also handle the case where ComponentPropsWithoutRef
appears inside an intersection type alias, which was causing it to be
treated as opaque when it should expand the HTML attributes.
```

## Releases

Add a changeset for a consumer-visible change (`.changeset/`; see `AGENTS.md` for how to write one). Callisto (version pinned in `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`) plans the versions from the changesets and opens a release pull request (`callisto/version-packages`); merging it runs `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`, which publishes the crates and npm packages, tags each package, and publishes one GitHub Release for the CLI (`cargo/caliper-docgen@x.y.z`) with its changelog section as the notes and the five CLI binaries attached, each with a build attestation. The npm wrapper's tag `npm/caliper-docgen@x.y.z` is what the tap reads. `docs/releasing.md` has the release flow and how to recover a failed run.

Homebrew pulls from us: the tap's daily `brew bump` finds that tag with `livecheck`, builds `crates/cli` from source and bottles it, and a maintainer merges the formula pull request. Nothing in this repository notifies the tap.

Speed, memory and accuracy are recorded weekly and compared with the previous run (`docs/measurement.md`); there is no pull-request gate. Run `just bench` when a change touches the resolver.

## Pull requests

1. Branch from `main`
2. Keep the pre-commit hook passing
3. Update snapshots if extraction output changes (`cargo insta review`)
4. One logical change per PR — squash fixup commits before merging

> `just bench` is a local check of speed and memory against `main`; it prints a table and fails nothing. Accuracy against RDT and react-docgen is tracked by the weekly record (`docs/measurement.md`), not by a pull-request gate.

## Local disk, caches and worktrees

Each place holds one kind of thing, and its name says which.

- **The repository:** code we re-run (`scripts/`, `apps/oracle`), decisions (`docs/adr/`), process (this file, `AGENTS.md`), and small test inputs (`fixtures/`). Anything a later change or a reviewer needs goes here, or in the pull request description.
- **Caches you can delete at any time:** `target/`, `node_modules/`, and `.corpora/` (the weekly's pinned repos, gitignored; `docs/measurement.md`). Deleting one costs rebuild or download time and nothing else. A worktree's `target/` was about 5 GB and its `node_modules/` about 400 MB when this was written.
- **Throwaway output:** logs, A/B binaries, diffs. Write them under `$TMPDIR`, which is not kept. If you need a result later, record it in the pull request or in `docs/`.
- **Nothing outside the repository is kept for the project.** Do not create a directory under `~/Projects` for output, and do not store build output in a directory named for something else (a `fixtures` directory holds test inputs only).

`just test-checker-lane` builds into `target/release` of the current checkout and reads the binary from there, so run it without `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` set.

Each worktree has its own `target/`, `node_modules/` and `.corpora/`. To share one copy of the corpora between worktrees, pass `--corpora DIR` to `scripts/corpora.py` and `scripts/weekly.py`. Keep few worktrees: after a branch is merged and pushed, remove its worktree (`git worktree remove`), delete the local branch, and run `git worktree prune`.

## Before you push a behavior change

`just lint doc-check machete typos` must pass, plus the tests of the crates you touched. CI runs the rest. A change that decides something about types or props (relevance, resolution, merging) also needs:

- **Invariants:** state them in the pull request description: unknown unless proven, by binding and not by spelling, every read recorded, one owner for each decision, wired or not defined.
- **Allow-lists:** a guard handles a closed set of proven forms, and everything else is unknown or declined, never "complete", "none" or "exact". No `_ =>` arm in a decision over node or type kinds.
- **Grammar sweep:** list every syntax or type form the code can receive and show each is handled or declined. Prefer a generated test over the grammar with the TypeScript checker as the oracle (`crates/semantic/tests/`) to a hand-picked list. Cover lone surrogates, computed keys, shadowing, `declare`, overloads and re-exports.
- **Mutation proof:** remove each guard in turn; a test must fail. `cargo mutants --in-diff <diff>` finds the ones no test notices.
- **A test that fails on `main`** for every behavior change.
- **Output-preserving change:** diff `extract --json --quiet --no-cache` against a build of `main` on a large project and on Chakra, with `stats` removed. For resolver or checker changes, also compare peak memory and time with `just bench`, because a size regression can pass every test.
- **Findings:** when an automated or human review finds a defect, fix the class it belongs to, not only the case, and resolve the finding with the commit and test that fix it.

## Snapshot tests

# Contributing

By participating in this project, you agree to abide by the [Code of Conduct](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). Found a security issue? See [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md) instead of opening a public issue.

## Prerequisites

| Tool  | Min version   | Notes                                         |
| ----- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| Rust  | 1.99          | `rustup update stable`                        |
| proto | latest        | manages Node/pnpm versions from `.prototools` |
| pnpm  | `.prototools` | via proto, or `npm i -g pnpm`                 |

After installing proto, run `moon setup` once to pull the pinned Node version and any other tool versions declared in `.prototools`.

## Build & test

```bash
# Rust
cargo build                                            # dev build
cargo test -p caliper-docgen-core                   # unit + snapshot tests
cargo clippy -p caliper-docgen-core -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all

# TypeScript
pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin test      # unit tests (mocked NAPI)
pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin test:integration  # integration tests (real native binding)

# Speed and memory of your branch against origin/main (Mantine and Chakra)
just bench
```

The pre-commit hook runs `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings`, `typos`, and `cargo deny` on every commit. It's fast enough that skipping it isn't worth the trouble.

## Snapshot tests

Snapshot tests use [insta](https://insta.rs). Each fixture (shadcn, MUI, Chakra, etc.) has a snapshot of the full extraction output. If your change touches extraction output, insta will flag it:

```bash
cargo test -p caliper-docgen-core    # fails with "snapshot mismatch"
cargo insta review                     # review diffs, accept or reject
```

Accept any snapshot change that is intentional (i.e., the output got more accurate). Reject regressions.

## Where code goes

**`crates/core`** — everything that understands TypeScript ASTs and React component patterns. No I/O, no async, no terminal output. Every function here must be `Send + Sync` so rayon can parallelize it.

**`crates/cli`** — user-facing output only. No extraction logic. Commands parse args and delegate to `core::pipeline`. Error formatting uses `miette`; progress uses `indicatif`; table output uses `comfy-table`.

**`crates/binding`** — thin NAPI wrapper. Owns the async runtime (tokio) and exposes the NAPI functions listed in `packages/napi/binding.d.ts` (batch extraction, sessions, and the lazy session's index, answers and warm-up). No business logic.

**`packages/napi`** — `caliper-docgen-napi`. TypeScript types (`index.d.ts`) and the dev binary loader (`index.js`) that finds the `.node` file from `target/` or `NAPI_RS_NATIVE_LIBRARY_PATH`. No logic.

**`packages/vite-plugin`** — `caliper-docgen-vite-plugin`. Single Vite `Plugin` object. No extraction logic — calls NAPI and manages HMR.

## Code style

The authoritative reference is `.claude/skills/rust-style/SKILL.md`. Highlights:

**Maps:** `FxHashMap` for internal maps (hot path, no DoS surface). `BTreeMap` for anything that ends up in JSON output (key ordering must be deterministic and stable across runs).

**Strings:** `CompactString` for type names and prop names. Most are ≤24 bytes (`string`, `boolean`, `ReactNode`, `MouseEvent`) and fit inline without heap allocation.

**Control flow:** `let...else` keeps the happy path flat:

```rust
let Some(entry) = map.get(key) else { return None };
```

**Matching on project-local enums:** no wildcards. `match status { Ok => .., Err => .. }` gives a compile error when new variants are added. `match status { Ok => .., _ => .. }` silently ignores them.

**No `unwrap()` outside tests.** Use `?` or emit a `Diagnostic` and return a safe default. The `Diagnostic` type has constructors for common error shapes.

**Comments:** only when the WHY is non-obvious. Not what the code does.

## Commits

- GPG-signed, `Signed-off-by` trailer (both configured in `.git/config`). `main` requires signed commits, so an unsigned commit in a pull request blocks the merge.
- `feat:` / `fix:` / `refactor:` / `chore:` / `docs:` prefix
- No line wrapping at any column
- Subject line says it all — skip the body if it adds nothing

```
# good
feat: resolve ComponentPropsWithoutRef in intersection type aliases

# bad
Updated the resolver to also handle the case where ComponentPropsWithoutRef
appears inside an intersection type alias, which was causing it to be
treated as opaque when it should expand the HTML attributes.
```

## Releases

Add a changeset for a consumer-visible change (`.changeset/`; see `AGENTS.md` for how to write one). Callisto (version pinned in `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`) plans the versions from the changesets and opens a release pull request (`callisto/version-packages`); merging it runs `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`, which publishes the crates and npm packages, tags each package, and publishes one GitHub Release for the CLI (`cargo/caliper-docgen@x.y.z`) with its changelog section as the notes and the five CLI binaries attached, each with a build attestation. The npm wrapper's tag `npm/caliper-docgen@x.y.z` is what the tap reads. `docs/releasing.md` has the release flow and how to recover a failed run.

Homebrew pulls from us: the tap's daily `brew bump` finds that tag with `livecheck`, builds `crates/cli` from source and bottles it, and a maintainer merges the formula pull request. Nothing in this repository notifies the tap.

Speed, memory and accuracy are recorded weekly and compared with the previous run (`docs/measurement.md`); there is no pull-request gate. Run `just bench` when a change touches the resolver.

## Pull requests

1. Branch from `main`
2. Keep the pre-commit hook passing
3. Update snapshots if extraction output changes (`cargo insta review`)
4. One logical change per PR — squash fixup commits before merging

> `just bench` is a local check of speed and memory against `main`; it prints a table and fails nothing. Accuracy against RDT and react-docgen is tracked by the weekly record (`docs/measurement.md`), not by a pull-request gate.

## What

Two sections in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, from the worker rules that lived only outside the repository.

- **Local disk, caches and worktrees:** what the repository holds, what is a cache you can delete (`target/`, `node_modules/`, `.corpora/`), where throwaway output goes (`$TMPDIR`), that nothing outside the repository is kept for the project, how to share one corpora copy between worktrees (`--corpora DIR`), and when to remove a worktree. It also says to run `just test-checker-lane` without `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, because the recipe reads `target/release` of the checkout.
- **Before you push a behavior change:** the bar for changes that decide something about types or props. Invariants in the description, allow-list guards, a grammar sweep with the TypeScript checker as oracle, a mutation proof (`cargo mutants --in-diff`), a test that fails on `main`, an output diff and a memory and time check for resolver changes, and fixing the class of a finding, not the case.

## Evidence

- `just lint doc-check machete typos`: exit 0.
- Checked against the repository: `scripts/corpora.py` and `scripts/weekly.py` both take `--corpora` and default to `.corpora/repos` under the checkout (`ROOT` is the directory above `scripts/`); `.corpora/`, `target/` and `node_modules/` are gitignored; `just bench` exists.
- The 5 GB and 400 MB figures are from one worktree measured on 2026-11-17 (4.7 GB `target/`, about 400 MB `node_modules/`).

## Not verified

- No code changes, so no behavior to test.
- I did not check that every sentence of the bar matches what CI enforces; it is the standard reviewers apply, not a gate.
- The acceptance harness used to compare Controls rows and the oracle headline is not in the repository and is not described here. It was in a directory that has been deleted.

**Done:**

The second is the pre-push bar for behavior changes: allow-list guards, grammar sweep, mutation proof, and fixing the class of a finding. `just lint doc-check machete typos` passes, and the body is published.
- **`docs/measurement.md` already documents the weekly oracle and the pinned corpora**, so it needs nothing from the deleted directory.
- **Worktrees removed:**
  - `dep-502`, which was clean.
  - `mf-t4`, which held only a Playwright log and one screenshot.

**Not done:**

It holds only a 440 KB untracked `.scratch/` of worker edit scripts, nothing tracked. I did not work around the denial. If you're fine with it, remove it with `! git worktree remove --force /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper/.claude/worktrees/agent-ae96c08e3c3bf7d68`.

**Next, in the order I'd do it:**
1. **Change 8** (no analysable body means unknown, so MUI `.d.ts` components keep `className`, `style` and `ref`), as one PR off main.

4. **The `~/.cache/caliper/corpora` and `sccache` questions,** which are yours to decide.

content.text:
Change 8 is in progress. It is reproduced at current main but not yet confirmed against the pre-#490 baseline, which is building in the background (about 4 minutes).

**What I've found so far (MUI `Button` fixture, default settings):**
- `Button` is a `declare const` with no function body, so relevance has no evidence about how it uses its props and its `body` is `None`.
- It keeps `ref` among its 26 rows. `className` and `style` are not rows, and the 288-member `React.ButtonHTMLAttributes` layer is collapsed with 0 used.
- With `--html-attributes curated` it is the same (160 members, 0 used).

**The fix I'm planning:**
- A component with no analysable body gives relevance nothing to narrow by. I'd carry a "listed by the structural answer" flag on each member, and in `decide` leave a member alone when the body is `None` and the structural answer already listed it.
- This is the "unknown unless proven" rule for a missing body, and it needs no name lists.
- It covers MUI's `.d.ts` components, though `Button` and `Select` also have a separate extraction gap I'll report on afterwards.

**One check before I write code:** whether the pre-#490 baseline really listed `className` and `style` for these components. If it didn't, then change 8 is only about `ref`, or isn't needed. I'll compare the two builds when the baseline finishes and tell you which it is before I change anything.

content.text:
I haven't changed any code for change 8, because the evidence turns it into a product decision that is yours.

**What I measured** (MUI `Button` fixture, a `declare const`, so no function body):
- **Before #490, default settings:** 310 rows, including `className`, `style` and `ref`.
- **Before #490, curated mode (the addon's real shape):** 25 rows plus 161 curated attributes, including `className`, `style` and `ref`. That large listing was the noise you wanted gone.
- **At current main:** 26 rows. `ref` stays. `className` and `style` are gone, because the 160 ambient attributes are names in a collapsed layer with none used.

The loss is real, but it is the rule from #490 working as designed: an ambient member is a name unless the body uses it. A body-less component has no body to read, so nothing earns it a row, and the same would be true of a source component whose body ignores `className`.

**The question is what unknown should mean for a component with no analysable body.** Three options, and I recommend the first:
1. **Leave it as is, and say so plainly.** `className` and `style` stay names in a layer for body-less components. The Controls count stays low (26 for `Button`). I'd add a note to the output that the body wasn't analysed, so the gap is stated and not silent. This fits "ambient stays as names" and the "plain statements of what's missing" goal.
2. **Restore the curated subset for body-less components.** That brings back about 160 rows for a MUI `Button`, which is the noise you rejected. Every `.d.ts` library, which is most real design systems, would get it.
3. **Restore a small set, such as `className`, `style` and `ref`.** This would need a name list, which breaks "decide by provenance, never by name lists".

**What I don't know:** the handoff described change 8 as "no analysable body = unknown, keep what main listed", but the evidence behind it was in `pattern-eval.md`, which is gone. So I can't tell whether you wanted option 2 or 3. If you want either, say which and I'll implement it with a test that fails on main.

I'll hold change 8 until you answer, and meanwhile look at change 7 (a `useX(props)` hand-off counts as forwarding), which I think is independent of this.

content.text:
Change D has a diagnosed root cause and a tested fix, still uncommitted. The main build for comparison is running in the background.

**Root cause (Chakra fixture, 878 rows per `Button`):** about 850 of those rows were csstype style interfaces, reached through `React.CSSProperties`. The checker reads them; the structural lane never does. The checker merge only turns a source it alone found into a layer when it "proved the props type reaches it whole". Its walk stopped at every `@types/react` type, so that proof failed and "never hide on silence" listed all of them. So the `declined` guard was not the cause for this shape.

**Fix:** `composes` in `crates/semantic/src/convert.rs` now keeps walking a React type's bases. It names no extra React types, and a base the checker can't be asked for leaves those sources unproven, as before. `Button` went from 878 to 236 rows, with `VendorLonghandProperties` (224 names) and `StandardLonghandProperties` (370 names) as layers.

**Test:** `a_source_only_a_react_type_reaches_collapses_like_any_other_large_source`, built on the real `fixtures/chakra/Button.d.ts`. It passes with the fix and fails with the fix disabled. My first two test shapes passed on main too; the structural lane already handles those, so I switched to the fixture file. The test harness needed a `load_dependencies` option, added as `both_lanes_loading`.

**Remaining (about 212 rows):**
- Smaller csstype sources of 107, 76 and 26 members stay listed. They fall under the existing per-source thresholds (30 for ambient sources, 200 otherwise).
- Fixing that would mean treating a source reached only through a React type as ambient, which changes the rule in `types/ambient.rs`. It also touches the parity test against the oracle's classifier. I haven't done it.
- About 50 more rows are names React's own attribute interfaces also declare (`color`, `cursor`, `display`). The merge keeps those deliberately.

**Still to do before pushing:**
- The lint gate, workspace nextest and the checker lane.
- Output diff and memory/time against main on the fixtures.
- `/code-review medium`.

I deleted the temporary `fixtures/_tmp_styled` after use; checking that now along with the gate.

Triage of the seven review items, against the code:

- **Extra RPCs per React type:** real cost, but small; the fixtures run showed no time change. I can only measure it fully on real corpora.
- **Unknown bases dropped silently:** not a hide. A source that is never reached is never in `whole`, so the merge lists it. That is the safe direction.
- **`known &= below_react`:** harmless but obscure. I'll make it explicit.
- **`names` ordering:** a below-React visit pushes no names, so the order of direct visits is unchanged.
- **Brittle test:** fair. I'll identify csstype by file path instead of interface names.
- **`both_lanes` wrapper:** style only; keeping it avoids touching nine call sites.
- **Stale doc wrapping:** fair; fixing.

input.content:
## What

A component whose props type reaches csstype through `React.CSSProperties` listed every csstype member as a row. The checker merge turns a source only the checker found into a layer of names only when the checker proved the props type reaches it whole, and the walk (`composes` in `crates/semantic/src/convert.rs`) stopped at every `@types/react` type, so csstype's interfaces under `CSSProperties` were never proven whole. "Never hide on silence" then listed them: on the Chakra fixture, `Button` had 878 rows, about 850 of them csstype's.

The walk now keeps going into a React type's bases, on the same edges that keep every member, and names no further React types. `Button` has 236 rows; `VendorLonghandProperties` (224 names) and `StandardLonghandProperties` (370) are layers.

Invariants: unknown unless proven (a React type whose bases cannot be asked for proves nothing, so what is beneath it stays listed); a source is reached whole only through the edges that keep every member (a `Pick` still selects); the `names` list is unchanged (a visit below a React type pushes none).

## Evidence

- `a_source_only_a_react_type_reaches_collapses_like_any_other_large_source` (crates/semantic/tests/relevance_model.rs), on the real `fixtures/chakra/Button.d.ts`: passes with the fix, fails with the walk into a React type's bases disabled. It finds csstype by file path, not interface names.
- `just lint doc-check machete typos`: exit 0. `cargo nextest run` on the touched crates: 1515 passed. `just test-checker-lane`: exit 0.
- Output against main on all of `fixtures/` (`extract --json`, `stats` dropped): only the 8 Chakra fixture components differ; the other 44 are identical.
- Peak RSS on `fixtures/` (4 interleaved runs, load 36 to 42): main 204 to 210 MiB, this change 194 to 195 MiB; time equal within noise.
- `/code-review medium` on origin/main..HEAD: 7 items; fixed the stale doc wrapping, the obscure `known` update and the test's reliance on csstype's interface names; the rest were checked against the code and need no change (an unreached source is listed, which is the safe direction).

## Not verified

- No measurement on a real corpus (Chakra, Mantine, MUI, antd): none is cloned. The walk now asks the checker for the bases of each React type it meets, which costs a few extra requests per component; the fixtures show no time change, a large project may.
- About 212 rows of the Chakra fixture's `Button` remain from smaller csstype interfaces (107, 76, 26 and 3 members), under the per-source thresholds (30 ambient, 200 otherwise), and about 50 from names React's own attribute interfaces also declare. Treating a source reached only through a React type as ambient would collapse more; it changes `types/ambient.rs` and its parity test, and is not part of this change.
- Whether `StandardLonghandProperties` and the like stay the sources csstype splits `Properties` into in other csstype versions: the test does not depend on it.
